pub_desc: Publications (articles, reports, book chapters) reporting empirical or theoretical work on public attitudes, perceptions, opinions and discourse about refugees and asylum seekers in Germany, Europe, or comparative contexts.
pub_narr: Include publications that present surveys, qualitative studies, media analyses or policy research explicitly about attitudes toward refugees/asylum seekers, acceptance, integration preferences, perceived threat, xenophobia, support for refugee-related policies, or changes in public opinion over time. Include works that analyse determinants (contact, political ideology, media exposure), subgroup differences, and longitudinal trends. Exclude publications that only address migration in general without specific attention to refugees/asylum seekers, studies solely about migration policy mechanics without public opinion, or historical/descriptive pieces that do not address attitudes or opinions.

pub_desc: Publications addressing general life satisfaction or global subjective well‑being, including measurement, determinants, cross‑national comparisons, and longitudinal changes.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies that explicitly measure or analyse overall life satisfaction (single‑item global measures or validated scales), their correlates (income, health, social relations, employment), measurement properties, and population-level trends. Include comparative work using ESS, WVS, SOEP or other survey data. Exclude publications focused solely on domain-specific satisfaction (e.g., job satisfaction, marital satisfaction) unless they include a global life satisfaction measure or directly compare domain and global measures.

pub_desc: Publications on general self‑efficacy (self‑perceived competence to cope with life’s demands), including psychometric studies, validations, correlational and intervention research.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical work that uses or evaluates general self‑efficacy constructs (e.g., General Self‑Efficacy Scale), cross‑cultural validations, associations with health, education, employment and wellbeing, and interventions aimed at changing general self‑efficacy. Exclude studies focused exclusively on domain‑specific self‑efficacy (academic, health, occupational) unless a general self‑efficacy measure is also included.

pub_desc: Publications examining antisemitism: prevalence, attitudes, stereotypes, conspiracy beliefs, historical and contemporary manifestations, hate crimes and policy responses.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, surveys, qualitative analyses and reports that explicitly measure or theorize antisemitic attitudes, incidents, discourse, causes and consequences. Include research on measurement (scales), demographic correlates, intergroup dynamics, and evaluations of interventions or policies addressing antisemitism. Exclude general prejudice research that does not include antisemitic-specific measures or analyses, and works that only discuss Jewish history without linking to contemporary antisemitic attitudes or incidents.

pub_desc: Publications on work and employment: labor market participation, job quality, unemployment, employment transitions, workplace conditions and labour market policy evaluations.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies that focus on employment status, job characteristics (hours, contract type, sector), unemployment/incidence, underemployment, labor market integration, returns to work, and policy impacts (active labour market programmes, minimum wage). Include research on subpopulations (youth, migrants, disabled) if employment is the central focus. Exclude publications that concern education, training, or retirement solely in non‑employment contexts unless linked to employment outcomes.

pub_desc: Publications addressing occupational load, work-related stress, psychosocial and physical burdens at work, and their effects on health, safety, performance, and absenteeism.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, and theoretical work that focus on workload, job strain, psychosocial risk factors (e.g. demands, control, effort-reward imbalance), occupational stress, burnout related to paid work, and interventions to reduce work-related burden. Include workplace health and safety reports, epidemiological studies linking work exposures to health outcomes, and policy analyses about occupational risk. Exclude publications on non-work-related stress (purely family or general life stress without workplace linkage), student academic workload unless explicitly framed as employment, and purely economic analyses of labor markets that do not address occupational burden or psychosocial/physical working conditions.

pub_desc: Publications on job satisfaction, employee attitudes toward work, facets of satisfaction (pay, supervision, tasks), and links with performance, turnover, and well‑being.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical papers, and reviews that investigate overall job satisfaction or its components, determinants (e.g. job characteristics, rewards, leadership), outcomes (e.g. commitment, turnover intentions, productivity), and interventions to improve satisfaction. Include cross-national and sector-specific studies of satisfaction and measurement research about satisfaction scales. Exclude studies focused solely on customer satisfaction, student satisfaction unrelated to employment, or organizational climate papers that do not report job satisfaction measures.

pub_desc: Publications on work in the context of enterprises and firms: workplace organization, industrial relations, employment practices, production processes, and company-level working conditions.
pub_narr: Include studies and reports that examine the relationship between work and the employing organization such as organizational structure, HR practices, workplace governance, industrial relations, occupational safety at the firm level, production organization, and case studies of companies. Include comparative studies of establishments, employer surveys, and policy analyses concerning workplace and firm practices. Exclude macroeconomic labor market analyses that do not address firm- or establishment-level work processes, and purely consumer-focused business research unrelated to employee work.

pub_desc: Publications about work–life relations: work–family balance, reconciliation of employment and private life, flexible work arrangements, and effects on well‑being and family outcomes.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies that investigate work–life balance, work–family conflict and enrichment, flexible working time, parental leave, telework and its effects on family life, and policies to reconcile work and private life. Include comparative policy analyses, interventions, and qualitative studies of lived experience. Exclude publications focusing exclusively on family dynamics without connection to employment, or on retirement and leisure that do not consider work–life interaction.

pub_desc: Publications covering employment, work organisation, occupations, labour relations, job quality, occupational health, and the sociology/economics of work.
pub_narr: Include broad empirical studies, reviews, and theoretical work about paid work and employment: labor market participation, occupational structure, working conditions, job quality, employment relations, skills and training, occupational health and safety, and policy interventions affecting work. Include sectoral, cross-national, and historical perspectives on work. Exclude content unrelated to employment (e.g. volunteer activities unless explicitly analyzed as work) and publications that do not address work or employment dimensions.

pub_desc: Publications analyzing the changing nature of work and employment over time, including causes, patterns and consequences of structural, technological and organizational change.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical and theoretical studies, review articles and policy reports that address transformations in work (e.g. digitalization, automation, platform work, flexibilization, demographic change), longitudinal analyses of occupational change, comparative/historical accounts of labor market restructuring, and evaluations of policies responding to change. Include works at micro (worker, firm), meso (occupation, sector) and macro (national, cross-national) levels. Exclude: publications that only mention the phrase without analysing change; narrow technical papers on specific technologies that do not address effects on work or employment; purely clinical or medical case reports unrelated to labor-market transformation.

pub_desc: Publications on work and occupations covering job characteristics, occupational choice, career development, vocational training and the labour market role of occupations.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical studies, theoretical analyses and reviews that address occupations, career trajectories, vocational education & training, job characteristics, occupational segregation, sectoral differences, and labour market outcomes by profession. Include cross-sectional and longitudinal research, policy analyses and comparative studies. Exclude: papers solely about leisure or unrelated personal activities; studies that use 'occupation' only as a demographic label without substantive analysis of work or occupational processes.

pub_desc: Publications investigating work and job satisfaction, including determinants, consequences, measurement and cross-group comparisons of occupational well-being.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical studies, theoretical papers, meta-analyses and policy reports on job/organizational satisfaction, its antecedents (job characteristics, working conditions, leadership, pay), consequences (health, turnover, productivity), and measurement approaches. Include research on intrinsic/extrinsic satisfaction, cross-national comparisons and sectoral studies. Exclude: works that only mention satisfaction in passing without measurement or analysis, and studies focused on life satisfaction without connection to job-related satisfaction.

pub_desc: Publications on working conditions, including physical, psychosocial, contractual and temporal aspects of work and their impacts on health, safety and well-being.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical research, reviews and policy analyses addressing occupational health and safety, psychosocial risks, work organisation, shift work, working hours, job control, workplace hazards, precarious contracts, and their effects on workers. Include intervention and evaluation studies, sector-specific analyses, and cross-national comparisons. Exclude: publications that only use the term superficially without analysing working conditions, and papers exclusively about non-work settings.

pub_desc: Publications on unemployment, including its causes, duration, socio-economic consequences and policy responses at individual and population levels.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical analyses, theoretical studies, policy reports and reviews addressing unemployment incidence, long-term unemployment, youth unemployment, unemployment duration and transitions, unemployment benefits and active labour market policies, and the socio-economic and health impacts of joblessness. Include cross-national comparisons and administrative-data based studies. Exclude: studies that only mention unemployment tangentially (e.g. as a control variable) without substantive analysis.

pub_desc: Publications that study commuting/to-work journeys (Arbeitsweg), including travel time, mode choice, distance, congestion, active commuting, and health or wellbeing consequences of commuting.
pub_narr: Include empirical articles, reports and reviews that focus on the daily journey to and from work: determinants of commute mode, commute duration, spatial distance, multimodal trips, peak-hour dynamics, commuting-related stress, injury or exposure en route, and links between commuting and health, productivity or work–life balance. Also include urban planning and transport policy evaluations that target commuting. Exclude publications that treat non-work travel in general without distinguishing trips to/from workplace, or publications that only mention commuting peripherally without measured or analyzed commuting variables.

pub_desc: Publications on working time (Arbeitszeit): hours of work, schedules, shift work, overtime, flexible hours, part-time/full-time distinctions, and related policy and health outcomes.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, policy analyses and reviews examining contractual and actual working hours, temporal organization of work (shifts, night work, irregular schedules), overtime and unpaid hours, effects on health, wellbeing and family life, productivity, and legal/regulatory frameworks for working time. Exclude publications that focus solely on non-labour temporal measures (e.g., leisure time only) or that mention hours worked without analysis or measurement.

pub_desc: Publications addressing foreigners/immigrants (Ausländer): migration status, integration, labour market outcomes, health disparities, discrimination, and demographic studies of foreign-born populations.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical works that explicitly study foreign-born persons, migrants, or persons with migration background: labor market integration, educational attainment, health and wellbeing among migrants, social inclusion/exclusion, legal and policy analysis of immigration, and statistical descriptions of foreign populations. Include studies that use the term 'Ausländer' in context of nationality, citizenship or migration background. Exclude works that use the term only in passing, studies focused solely on tourists or short-term visitors, or publications that do not disaggregate by migration status or country of origin.

pub_desc: Publications on burdens arising from work (Belastung von Arbeit), including psychosocial stressors, workload, physical load, occupational hazards, burnout and health consequences of work demands.
pub_narr: Include empirical and review studies that analyze how aspects of work create burden—psychosocial demands (workload, time pressure, emotional demands), physical strain (ergonomic load, repetitive movements), exposure to hazards, and resulting outcomes such as stress, burnout, musculoskeletal disorders, sickness absence or reduced well‑being. Include occupational health interventions addressing reduction of work-related burden. Exclude studies concerning non-work stressors unless they explicitly connect to or confound work-related burden.

pub_desc: Publications exploring the relationship between burden/stress (Belastung) and work (Arbeit): how work produces burden and how burden affects work performance, health and employment outcomes.
pub_narr: Include research examining causal or associative links between work conditions and burdens (physical, mental, psychosocial), effects of burden on productivity, absenteeism and career trajectories, and interventions to mitigate work-related burden. Accept interdisciplinary studies (occupational health, psychology, sociology, labour economics) that explicitly analyze the interplay between burden and work. Exclude literature that treats burden or work independently without analysis of their connection.

pub_desc: Publications addressing physical, ergonomic, psychosocial and organizational workplace burdens, exposures and their health or productivity consequences.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and reports that examine workplace stressors, ergonomic loads, psychosocial demands (e.g., job strain, effort-reward imbalance), physical hazards (noise, chemicals, manual handling), injury and sickness absence related to work. Include intervention and evaluation studies that aim to reduce workplace burdens. Exclude studies that focus on non-workplace stress (domestic or community stress) unless explicitly linked to occupational exposures, and exclude purely clinical case reports not situated in workplace contexts.

pub_desc: Publications concerned with occupations, occupational classification, employment status and labor market roles.
pub_narr: Include studies, reports and analyses addressing job titles, occupational status, occupational stratification and their links to socioeconomic outcomes, health or mobility. Include methodological papers on occupation coding and classification. Exclude publications that do not pertain to occupational roles (e.g., unrelated uses of the word) or that treat employment only as a peripheral demographic variable without substantive occupational detail.

pub_desc: Publications examining the relationship between educational attainment, qualifications and occupational outcomes or career development.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies on how education influences occupational status, job matching, returns to education, vocational training, skill formation and social mobility. Include research on educational-occupational mismatch and transitions from education to employment. Exclude works that deal only with educational pedagogy without linking to occupational destinations or labor market outcomes.

pub_desc: Publications on job satisfaction, workplace well-being and their determinants and consequences.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and reports that measure overall and facet-specific job satisfaction, examine predictors (work conditions, pay, supervision, autonomy) and outcomes (turnover, health, productivity). Include cross-national comparisons and longitudinal analyses of job satisfaction. Exclude studies that only address general life satisfaction without linking responses to employment or that use job satisfaction as a minor control variable without substantive analysis.

pub_desc: Publications on employment activity, types of work tasks, labor force participation and occupational engagement.
pub_narr: Include studies and reports that describe patterns of occupational activity (full-time/part-time, task composition), employment participation across groups, job task analyses, and the relationship between ability/health and work activity. Include investigations of occupational roles over the life course and occupational transitions. Exclude studies focusing on non-occupational activities (leisure, household tasks) unless linked to paid employment.

pub_desc: Scholarly publications, reports and book chapters discussing occupational mobility, career mobility, job-to-job transitions, vertical/horizontal mobility and labor market mobility processes in individual life courses or across groups.
pub_narr: Relevant documents describe empirical or theoretical work on occupational mobility (intra- and inter-occupational moves), measurement and determinants of job changes, promotion/demotion, sectoral mobility, geographic mobility for work, career trajectories and labor market segmentation. Include comparative, longitudinal and life-course studies, policy analyses of mobility barriers, and methodological papers on mobility measurement (e.g., mobility matrices, status scales). Exclude works focused solely on general migration without link to employment, macroeconomic mobility of firms, purely economic mobility concepts not tied to individual careers, or pieces that only mention mobility tangentially without substantive treatment.

pub_desc: Publications on occupational/work-related attitudes: work values, job-related beliefs, attitudes toward employment, vocational orientations, work ethic, and employment-related norms and preferences.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies addressing attitudes toward work and occupation, such as work values, preference for job security vs. flexibility, attitudes to vocational training, occupational aspirations, job satisfaction as an attitudinal construct, and public attitudes toward occupations. Exclude publications solely about occupational structure, labor-market outcomes without attitudinal measures, or clinical personality literature that does not connect traits to job attitudes.

pub_desc: Research on the occupational or professional self: professional identity, vocational self-concept, occupational self-efficacy, career identity and the role of self-perception in occupational choices and career development.
pub_narr: Include studies on how individuals perceive their professional role (professional identity, centrality of work to the self), development of vocational self-concept over the life course, occupational self-efficacy and confidence in job-related competencies, and the link between self-concept and career behavior. Exclude general self-concept literature without occupational focus, clinical self-esteem studies unrelated to work, or papers about organizational identity (firm-level) rather than individual professional identity.

pub_desc: Publications addressing public evaluation of social policies: citizen attitudes toward welfare state programs, assessments of effectiveness and fairness of social policy, and scholarly analyses of policy acceptance and legitimacy.
pub_narr: Include empirical and normative studies measuring or theorizing how individuals and groups evaluate social policy instruments (e.g., pensions, unemployment benefits, healthcare, family policies), perceived effectiveness, satisfaction with social policy, and determinants of support or opposition. Include cross-national comparisons, surveys of public opinion, and impact analyses of policy reforms on public evaluations. Exclude technical policy design papers without public-evaluation data, or studies on fiscal sustainability without linking to public perceptions.

pub_desc: Research on supervisor–subordinate relationships: leader–member exchange, supervisory support, workplace relations with managers, mentoring and trust between employees and their supervisors.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies examining the quality and effects of relationships between employees and their immediate supervisors, including leader–member exchange (LMX), supervisory support, perceived fairness, trust, conflict, mentoring and feedback processes. Include outcomes such as job satisfaction, performance, turnover intentions, and well-being. Exclude studies focused only on broad leadership styles at the organizational level without attention to dyadic relationships, or historical/organizational structure analyses without interpersonal focus.

pub_desc: Publications (articles, books, reports, policy papers) in German or English focused on adult education, continuing education, lifelong learning, and adult learning policies and programs, especially in German-speaking contexts.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, literature reviews, program evaluations, policy analyses, and theoretical work that address adult education ('Bildung Erwachsen'), continuing vocational training, informal and non-formal learning in adulthood, participation barriers, adult learning outcomes, and policy frameworks in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, or comparative European studies. Prefer sources that explicitly discuss adult learners, adult educational institutions, adult pedagogy, vocational retraining, or lifelong learning strategies. Exclude publications solely about compulsory schooling, higher education for traditional-age students, child or adolescent education, and purely clinical education unrelated to adult learning (unless tied to adult training programs).

pub_desc: Publications in German or English on care work ('Care Arbeit'), including paid and unpaid caregiving, eldercare, childcare, domestic care, labor conditions in care sectors, gendered division of care, and care policy.
pub_narr: Include empirical research, policy analyses, labor studies, ethnographies, and comparative reports that focus on care work performed in households, care institutions, and formal care sectors. Relevant topics: care labor market, unpaid family caregiving, migrant care workers, working conditions, wages, care policies, gender inequalities, and care commodification. Prefer studies addressing Germany or other European contexts when tagged 'Care Arbeit'. Exclude publications solely about clinical health outcomes without focus on care labor, veterinary or non-human care contexts, or general labor topics not specifying care tasks.

pub_desc: Academic and policy publications reporting on attitudes, beliefs, perceptions, and public opinion regarding climate change, including determinants of concern, risk perception, behavioral intentions, and policy support.
pub_narr: Include quantitative and qualitative studies, reviews, and policy briefs that directly investigate public attitudes toward climate change, beliefs about causes and risks, climate change skepticism or denial, willingness to act, and support for mitigation/adaptation policies. Prefer works using survey data or experimental designs measuring attitudinal constructs. Exclude publications about climate science per se without social-attitudinal focus, or technical modeling of climate processes absent public opinion analysis.

pub_desc: Publications across social science and natural science that address climate change broadly: causes, impacts, mitigation, adaptation, climate policy, societal responses, and interdisciplinary studies linking physical climate data with social/economic outcomes.
pub_narr: Include peer-reviewed articles, technical reports, assessment reports, policy briefs, and interdisciplinary studies that analyze climate change science, impacts (environmental, economic, social), mitigation and adaptation strategies, public policy and governance, and socio-economic consequences. Prioritize works that present empirical evidence, model results, or policy evaluation. Exclude documents unrelated to anthropogenic climate change such as isolated weather reports or non-climate environmental topics unless explicitly tied to climate change.

pub_desc: Scholarly and policy publications analyzing conceptions, definitions, and lay/theoretical understandings of democracy, democratic values, legitimacy, democratic quality, and citizen perceptions of democratic principles.
pub_narr: Include theoretical work, comparative studies, empirical analyses, and survey-based research that explicitly examine how democracy is conceptualized (procedural vs substantive, liberal vs participatory), public conceptions of democracy, normative debates on democratic legitimacy, and links between conceptions and political behavior. Prioritize publications that operationalize or measure conceptions of democracy. Exclude works that discuss democratic institutions only in technical legal terms without engagement with conceptions or public understandings.

pub_desc: Publications examining individual or household decision-making, attitudes, and behaviors related to consumption and purchasing across channels and contexts.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies on consumer decision processes, buying behavior, brand loyalty, advertising effects, online shopping, impulse purchases, consumer satisfaction, and cross-cultural comparisons of consumption. Include marketing, psychology, and behavioral economics perspectives that directly address how consumers choose, evaluate, and use products or services. Exclude publications focused solely on firm-level financial performance, supply-chain logistics, macroeconomic demand forecasting without individual/household behavior, or purely producer/firm strategies that do not measure consumer responses.

pub_desc: Publications related to COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) including epidemiology, public health, social and economic impacts, and policy responses to the pandemic.
pub_narr: Include research on COVID-19 transmission, case studies, clinical outcomes, vaccination and vaccine hesitancy, public-health interventions (NPIs), health-system impacts, mental health consequences, economic and social effects of the pandemic, and evaluations of pandemic policy measures. Include multidisciplinary work (medical, epidemiological, social sciences) if explicitly about COVID-19. Exclude publications not about SARS-CoV-2 or the 2019–present pandemic (e.g., unrelated coronaviruses) unless they directly inform COVID-19 understanding.

pub_desc: Publications on democracy (demokratie) including democratic institutions, participation, democratization, and threats to democratic governance.
pub_narr: Include comparative and national studies on democratic institutions, electoral systems, party competition, citizen participation, trust in democracy, civil liberties, democratic backsliding, democratization processes, and normative theory of democracy. Include works in German and other languages if they address democracy-related topics. Exclude studies that use the term 'democracy' metaphorically in unrelated contexts (e.g., 'market democracy' without political-institutional analysis).

pub_desc: Publications on depressive disorders and depressive symptoms, covering epidemiology, diagnosis, etiology, treatment, and outcomes.
pub_narr: Include clinical and population-based studies of major depression, dysthymia, depressive symptomatology, risk and protective factors, psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy trials, longitudinal course of depression, comorbidity with other mental or physical disorders, and public-health impacts. Exclude papers that mention 'depression' only as a transient mood in non-clinical contexts without measurement or analysis of depressive symptoms/disorders.

pub_desc: Publications on digitalization and digital technologies, including digital economy, digital skills, e-government, digital education, and the social effects of digital transformation.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical work on adoption and impacts of digital technologies (internet, mobile, platforms, AI), digital policy, digital divides and inequality, digital labor, e-governance, online behaviors, and digital transformation in organizations and education. Exclude uses of 'digital' as a generic file format reference or unrelated technical mentions without social, economic, or institutional context.

pub_desc: Publications that address digital competence/digital skills: definitions, frameworks, assessments, education and workplace implications.
pub_narr: Include scholarly articles, books, reports and conference papers that define or operationalize 'digital competence' (e.g. DigComp and related frameworks), describe assessment instruments, present empirical measurements (student, teacher, worker populations), discuss training/interventions to improve digital skills, or evaluate outcomes of digital competence on learning and labor-market results. Include theoretical and review articles that synthesize constructs and measurement approaches. Include pieces in German and English and policy documents from education and labor agencies. Exclude publications that only discuss technical IT infrastructure, software development techniques or network engineering without addressing human skills, or that use the phrase solely in marketing contexts without conceptual or empirical content.

pub_desc: Publications on digitization and its effects on work: labor markets, job tasks, skills, organization and employment relations.
pub_narr: Include empirical, theoretical and policy publications examining how digitalization (automation, AI, ICT adoption, platform work) changes job content, task composition, required skills, employment levels, job quality, working conditions, and organizational practices. Include sectoral studies, comparative labor-market analyses, impact assessments, case studies of workplace digital transformation, and reviews. Include publications on regulation, social dialogue and policy responses. Exclude pieces that treat digitization only as background technological change without linking to work, or purely technical ICT research not addressing labor or organizational outcomes.

pub_desc: Publications specifically focused on digitalization at the workplace: implementation, effects on tasks, workers and management.
pub_narr: Include case studies, empirical research and reviews examining workplace-level digital transformation: adoption of digital tools, changes in workflows and task design, effects on employee skills, productivity, job satisfaction and health, managerial practices, and training. Include interventions to support digital transitions, change management studies, and sector-specific workplace analyses. Exclude general theoretical discussions of digitization without workplace focus or studies limited to consumer digital adoption.

pub_desc: Publications on the relationship between digitization and work broadly, including labor market, occupational and organizational perspectives.
pub_narr: Include research that links digitalization processes to changes in employment, job content, skills demand, workplace organization, occupational health and socio-economic inequalities. Accept cross-disciplinary work from economics, sociology, organizational studies, education and public policy that addresses digitization's consequences for work. Include empirical analyses, theoretical contributions and policy evaluations. Exclude materials that discuss digital technology in non-work contexts without drawing implications for labor or occupations.

pub_desc: Publications on discrimination in schools: evidence, mechanisms, interventions and policy relevant to students and school staff.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical analyses, literature reviews and policy reports examining discrimination in educational settings by race/ethnicity, migration background, gender, disability, socioeconomic status, religion, sexual orientation or other protected characteristics. Include research on discriminatory practices, teacher bias, tracking and streaming, exclusionary discipline, attainment gaps, segregated schooling, microaggressions and anti-discrimination interventions. Include evaluation studies of programs aimed at reducing discrimination and legal/policy analyses. Exclude documents about general bullying unless explicitly linked to discrimination categories, or studies focused on higher education admissions policies only if not connected to school-level discrimination.

pub_desc: Publications (articles, books, reports) addressing discrimination: its forms, causes, prevalence, policy responses, and impacts in social, labor, education, housing, health, and institutional contexts.
pub_narr: Relevant publications are empirical studies, reviews, theoretical works, and policy reports that explicitly investigate discrimination (diskriminierung) or related concepts such as exclusion, unequal treatment, bias, prejudice, or institutional discrimination. Included are works on discrimination on grounds of race/ethnicity, gender, age, disability, religion, migration status, sexual orientation, or other protected characteristics; research on measurement and methodology for discrimination; and evaluations of anti-discrimination policies and interventions. Exclude publications that merely mention the term without substantive analysis, works focused solely on general inequality without reference to discriminatory mechanisms, and items about biological/medical processes that do not address social discrimination.

pub_desc: Scholarly and policy publications on education: systems, attainment, access, inequality, pedagogy, labor market returns, and education policy at all levels (early childhood to adult education).
pub_narr: Relevant publications include empirical studies, theoretical analyses, evaluations, and policy reports focused on education topics such as school access, educational attainment, curriculum and pedagogy, teacher quality, educational inequality, special education, vocational training, higher education, lifelong learning, and education policy reforms. Include comparative and country-specific research, quantitative and qualitative studies, and research linking education to outcomes like earnings and social mobility. Exclude publications that refer to 'education' only metaphorically or peripherally, studies solely about non-educational organizations using 'education' as a label, and highly technical works in unrelated fields that use 'education' in a different sense.

pub_desc: Publications examining attitudes toward Islam and Muslims: public opinion studies, prejudice research, media discourse analyses, and studies on policy implications and social integration.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical works that explicitly measure or analyze attitudes toward Islam or Muslims ("Einstellung zum Islam"), including public opinion surveys, social-psychological studies on prejudice and Islamophobia, media and political discourse analyses, and research on the effects of attitudes on policy, discrimination, and social cohesion. Studies may focus on country-specific or cross-national comparisons, subgroups, or temporal change. Exclude publications that deal with theological scholarship about Islam without addressing public or social attitudes, and works that use 'Islam' only as a background descriptor without analyzing attitudes.

pub_desc: Publications on attitudes toward immigration/migrants: public opinion research, determinants of immigration attitudes, political consequences, and policy debates.
pub_narr: Include studies that investigate public attitudes toward immigration ("Einstellung zur Zuwanderung"), including support or opposition to immigration levels, attitudes toward specific immigrant groups, determinants of immigration attitudes (economic, cultural, security), media and political framing effects, and links to voting or policy preferences. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses, comparative studies, and evaluations of messaging interventions are relevant. Exclude works focused solely on migration flows, legal procedures, or migrants' own attitudes unless they pertain to public attitudes about immigration.

pub_desc: Publications analyzing attitudes toward foreigners: public opinion, prejudice toward non-nationals, social integration, and consequences for policy and discrimination.
pub_narr: Relevant publications explicitly study attitudes toward foreigners ("Einstellung zu Ausländern") or non-citizen groups, including social-psychological research on prejudice and xenophobia, surveys of public sentiment toward immigrants and foreign residents, analyses of determinants of xenophobic attitudes, and implications for social cohesion and policy. Include comparative and national studies, trend analyses, and works linking attitudes to discriminatory behaviors. Exclude studies about foreign policy or international relations that use 'foreigner' in a diplomatic or state-centric context without addressing public attitudes toward people.

pub_desc: Scholarly publications (articles, books, chapters, reports) analyzing attitudes toward 'foreigners', migrants, immigrants, or ethnic outgroups; includes theoretical and empirical studies in sociology, political science, social psychology, and migration studies.
pub_narr: Include works that empirically or theoretically address attitudes, opinions, stereotypes, prejudice, xenophobia, social distance, integration attitudes, or public opinion regarding 'foreigners' (Fremde) or immigrants. Relevant publications cover national or comparative studies, qualitative and quantitative analyses, longitudinal and cross-sectional research, policy reports, and literature reviews on immigrant attitudes. Exclude items that focus exclusively on unrelated meanings of 'Fremde' (e.g., literary uses without social-attitudinal analysis), studies on mobility or tourism that do not address attitudes toward outgroups, and purely biological/medical studies that do not examine social attitudes.

pub_desc: Research publications examining attitudes toward gender, gender roles, gender equality, sexism, and related normative beliefs across disciplines such as sociology, gender studies, psychology, and political science.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical publications on gender attitudes (attitudes about gender roles, gender equality in work/family/politics, gender ideology, sexism, and discrimination), comparative and national studies, longitudinal trends, and interventions to change gender attitudes. Exclude publications that use 'gender' solely as a demographic variable without analyzing attitudes, technical gender theory texts with no attitudinal focus, and medical/biological studies that do not engage with social attitudes.

pub_desc: Scholarly publications analyzing attitudes toward Islam and Muslims, Islamophobia, integration debates, and public opinion concerning Islam in societal and political contexts.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies on public attitudes toward Islam/Muslims, prejudice and discrimination against Muslims, media representation, political mobilization around Islam, and comparative research on Islam-related attitudes. Also include policy analyses and surveys of public opinion about Islamic practices and Muslim communities. Exclude theological treatises on Islam that do not address public attitudes, purely historical studies without connection to contemporary attitudes, and medical research unrelated to social perceptions.

pub_desc: Publications on employment, labor market dynamics, workplace policies, and employment-related outcomes in Poland, including comparative studies of the Polish labor market.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, policy reports, working papers, and books addressing employment rates, unemployment, labor force participation, job quality, informal employment, migration-for-work, youth employment, gendered employment patterns, and labor market reforms in Poland. Also include comparative European analyses where Poland is a focal case. Exclude publications about employment in other countries that merely mention Poland in passing, and studies unrelated to labor market or employment (e.g., general demographic history without labor analysis).

pub_desc: Scholarly works on alienation from work (Entfremdung der Arbeit), including theoretical treatments (Marxist and sociological), empirical studies of job alienation, and research on related constructs like meaning at work and disengagement.
pub_narr: Include theoretical analyses of work alienation (classical Marxist theory and modern revisions), empirical studies measuring dimensions of alienation (powerlessness, meaninglessness, isolation, self-estrangement), occupational studies, organizational psychology research on alienation and job satisfaction, and comparative labor studies. Exclude uses of 'alienation' unrelated to work (e.g., cultural alienation in a non-work context) unless explicitly linked to employment or occupational experience.

pub_desc: Publications addressing the natural, built and social environment, including environmental science, environmental policy, pollution, sustainability, environmental health, and environmental education.
pub_narr: Relevant publications report empirical studies, reviews, theory, policy analyses or evaluations focused on environmental topics: ecology, climate change, air/water/soil pollution, environmental policy and governance, sustainability transitions, environmental justice, urban and built environment studies, and environmental attitudes/behaviour. Include cross-disciplinary social science work that treats environmental outcomes or human–environment interactions as a principal focus. Exclude works that use 'environment' only metaphorically or as incidental context (e.g., generic organizational "work environment" references with no environmental or ecological content), unless the organizational environment is analyzed for environmental outcomes or sustainability.

pub_desc: Publications studying attitudes toward the environment: measurement, determinants, outcomes, cross-national comparisons, and links between attitudes and behaviour or policy support.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical publications that define, measure, validate or analyse environmental attitudes (e.g., concern for environment, ecological worldview, climate worry), including psychometric studies of scales, determinants (socio-demographic, cultural, political), and consequences for behaviour and policy preferences. Exclude texts that mention environmental attitude only peripherally or focus solely on objective environmental indicators without considering attitudes or perceptions.

pub_desc: Publications on Erziehung (upbringing, education, socialization): family socialization, parenting, early childhood education, formal education processes, and pedagogical theory, including German-language literature.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, theoretical works and reviews focusing on upbringing, parenting practices, childrearing, educational methods (Erziehung in German pedagogical sense), socialization processes, and comparative studies of educational systems. Include German-language publications and works that use 'Erziehung' as a primary concept. Exclude uses of 'Erziehung' in highly specialized non-pedagogical senses (e.g., historical usages unrelated to human development) or documents that only mention the term tangentially.

pub_desc: Publications on evaluation in social work (Evaluation Soziale Arbeit): program evaluation, outcome assessment, methods and best practices specific to social work practice and services, including German-language literature.
pub_narr: Include empirical evaluations of social work programs, methodological papers on evaluation design in social work, case studies, systematic reviews and theoretical contributions on measuring social work outcomes. Focus on works that address evaluation frameworks, indicators of client well‑being, fidelity, implementation, and effectiveness within social work contexts. Exclude generic program-evaluation literature with no application to social work or documents that only mention social work tangentially.

pub_desc: Publications examining external political efficacy: conceptualization, measurement, determinants, consequences for political behaviour, and cross-national comparisons.
pub_narr: Include theoretical and empirical studies that define and measure external political efficacy (the belief that political institutions and actors are responsive to citizens), its antecedents (trust, representation, media, socioeconomic status), and outcomes (participation, protest, policy support). Include scale development/validation papers and comparative research using national or cross-national survey data. Exclude works that only discuss internal efficacy or general political efficacy without separate treatment of external efficacy.

pub_desc: Studies and reports on family–work interactions, work–family conflict, parental employment, reconciliation policies, and employment patterns among parents.
pub_narr: Include publications (articles, books, reports, policy papers) that examine how family responsibilities and employment interact: parental employment trajectories, part‑time vs full‑time work, maternity/paternity leave, childcare use and access, flexible working arrangements, work–family conflict, employer practices affecting families, and cross‑national comparisons of family‑friendly labour policies. Include empirical studies, longitudinal analyses, and policy evaluations. Exclude works focused solely on unrelated labour market topics (e.g., unemployment without family context), purely clinical family therapy, or biological/fertility studies that do not address employment or reconciliation of work and family.

pub_desc: Research on the interplay between family life and career development: career trajectories of parents, gendered career outcomes, childcare effects on career progression, and organizational career policies.
pub_narr: Include publications that investigate how family formation, parenthood, and caregiving influence career paths, promotion chances, occupational mobility, earnings trajectories, and career interruptions. Also include employer and policy analyses addressing career support (mentoring, flexible schedules, parental leave impact on careers). Prioritize empirical longitudinal research, qualitative career histories, and comparative studies of career outcomes by family status. Exclude literature solely about family therapy, fertility biology, or career studies that do not consider family or caregiving factors.

pub_desc: Scholarly works on transformations in gender roles within families: changing division of labour, parental roles, gender role attitudes, and implications for family structure and policy.
pub_narr: Include publications that analyze shifts in gender norms and practices inside households: trends in fathers' involvement in childcare, women's labour market participation, negotiation of household tasks, couple dynamics, intergenerational changes in gender attitudes, and policy effects on gender role change. Include quantitative trend analyses, qualitative ethnographies, cross‑national comparisons, and theoretical work on gender and family change. Exclude studies that treat gender only biologically or that focus exclusively on non‑family institutional gender dynamics without linking to family life.

pub_desc: Broad literature on family: family structure, life course transitions, parenting, households, kinship, intergenerational relations, family policy, and demographic trends.
pub_narr: Include publications covering empirical and theoretical research on families and households: marriage/cohabitation, divorce/separation, fertility and childbearing, parenting practices, intergenerational support, household composition, kin networks, demographic change, family policy, and socioeconomic determinants of family outcomes. Include cross‑disciplinary work (sociology, demography, social policy, psychology) and both quantitative and qualitative studies. Exclude works that use 'family' only metaphorically or unrelated technical uses (e.g., mathematical families) and clinical case reports not addressing broader family processes.

pub_desc: Research at the intersection of family and gender: gendered family roles, parenting practices, division of labour, gender inequalities within households, and gendered effects of family policy.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical publications exploring how gender shapes family life and how family contexts shape gender relations: studies on maternal and paternal roles, gender gaps in earnings and care, negotiation of household tasks, gendered impacts of parenthood, intersectionality (race/class) in family gender dynamics, and evaluations of policies affecting gender equality in families. Prioritize works that explicitly analyze both family and gender dimensions. Exclude research addressing gender in non‑family institutions only, or family studies that ignore gendered processes.

pub_desc: Scholarly and policy publications that define, measure, compare or evaluate types of employment contracts and work arrangements (e.g., full-time, part-time, temporary/fixed-term, permanent, self-employed, gig work, on-call, zero-hours, agency work, telework). Includes comparative, historical, legal, labor-economics, and social policy studies addressing causes, consequences and measurement issues of different employment forms.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical articles, reviews and reports that explicitly focus on the classification, prevalence, determinants or outcomes of distinct forms of employment; papers that use international or national definitional frameworks (ILO, EU) or propose typologies of employment. Include studies of working hours, contract type, job tenure, precarious work and gig economy that report operational definitions. Exclude works that use 'form' in unrelated senses (e.g., corporate legal form, organizational form unrelated to individual employment contracts), publications solely about macroeconomic indicators without disaggregating employment types, or papers that only nominally mention employment form without measures or definitions.

pub_desc: German-language and bilingual publications on the relationship between leadership (Führung) and trust (Vertrauen) in organizations and groups: theoretical work and empirical studies examining trust in leaders, leader behaviors that foster trust, leader–member exchange, and organizational trust dynamics.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical articles, German-language dissertations, book chapters and reports that explicitly study how leadership affects trust (trust in managers, trust in leadership), or how trust shapes leadership effectiveness; includes studies using German samples or German-language measures. Include cross-cultural comparisons where leadership and trust constructs are central. Exclude works where 'Führung' refers to guided tours, instructions, or generic steering unrelated to leadership in social/organizational contexts, or publications that mention trust only tangentially.

pub_desc: Publications on leadership (Führung) in organizations, teams and political or social movements: theories of leadership, leadership styles (transformational, transactional, servant, authoritarian), leadership effectiveness, leadership development, and cross-cultural leadership studies. Includes German-language and international literature.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical studies, theoretical papers, reviews and practitioner reports that focus on leadership concepts, measurement, antecedents and outcomes at individual, team and organizational levels. Include work on leader traits, behaviors, situational leadership, leadership development programs and leadership assessment. Exclude uses of 'Führung' that refer to tours/guided visits, simple instructions, or non-social leadership contexts (e.g., device controls) that are unrelated to social influence or managerial roles.

pub_desc: Publications about gender roles and gender-role attitudes: theoretical and empirical studies on beliefs about appropriate behaviors, responsibilities and identities for genders; research on role socialization, division of labor, family roles, occupational gender norms and changes over time.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: papers, books and reports that measure, analyze or theorize gender role attitudes/identities (e.g., traditional vs. egalitarian role beliefs), their determinants and consequences. Include cross-national comparisons, longitudinal trend analyses and research using attitude scales. Exclude studies solely about biological sex differences without reference to socially prescribed roles, or uses of 'role' in contexts unrelated to gender norms.

pub_desc: Publications addressing gender as a social and identity category: studies of gender identity, gender expression, gendered inequalities (labor market, health, politics), gender theory, and intersectional analyses of gender with class, race, sexuality and age.
pub_narr: Relevant publications: empirical and theoretical works that explicitly engage with 'gender' as distinct from biological sex, including research on gender identity, norms, discrimination, policy impacts, and measurement issues. Include studies using gender-disaggregated data or gender-focused qualitative research. Exclude papers that use 'gender' interchangeably with 'sex' without conceptual clarity, or works that do not treat gender as an analytical focus.

pub_desc: Scholarly publications addressing the study of gender as a social, cultural, political and historical category, including feminist theory, masculinity studies, queer studies and intersectional analyses.
pub_narr: Include: peer‑reviewed articles, books, book chapters, review articles and conference papers that explicitly focus on gender (social constructions of sex, gender identities, gender inequality, gender policy, intersectionality). Relevant geographic or historical case studies are in scope. Exclude: purely biomedical or genetic studies of biological sex differences that do not treat gender as a social construct; popular media pieces, opinion blogs, and non‑scholarly content unless published in an academic venue.

pub_desc: Academic literature on the concept of general self‑efficacy: theoretical foundations, psychometric evaluations, applications and correlational/causal studies across populations.
pub_narr: Include: empirical studies, theoretical articles, literature reviews and meta‑analyses that explicitly discuss general self‑efficacy as a construct (e.g., Schwarzer & Jerusalem), its measurement, validity, cross‑cultural adaptations and links to outcomes (health, education, work). Exclude: studies that only address domain‑specific self‑efficacy (e.g., academic, sporting) unless they also include or compare a general self‑efficacy measure.

pub_desc: Research publications about Generation Y (Millennials): demographic, social, occupational, cultural and attitudinal studies that identify or analyze this birth cohort.
pub_narr: Include: empirical and theoretical works that explicitly focus on or identify Generation Y / Millennials (commonly born roughly 1980s–mid/late 1990s), covering topics such as labour market behavior, political attitudes, family formation, consumption, technology use and cohort comparisons. Exclude: generic youth studies without cohort specification and studies using different cohort labels unless they clearly overlap and map to Generation Y by birth years.

pub_desc: German and international publications on general self‑efficacy (generelle Selbstwirksamkeit), covering theory, measurement, validation and applied research.
pub_narr: Include: German‑language and translated studies that explicitly treat 'generelle Selbstwirksamkeit' or the General Self‑Efficacy construct (e.g., Schwarzer & Jerusalem German version), psychometric evaluations, and applied research linking it to outcomes. Exclude: publications dealing only with context‑specific Selbstwirksamkeit (e.g., schulische Selbstwirksamkeit) unless they also address the general construct.

pub_desc: Scholarly works on sex/gender and gender roles (geschlecht und Geschlechterrollen), including studies of role expectations, socialization, division of labour and normative gender behaviour.
pub_narr: Include: empirical and theoretical literature on gender roles, role socialization, attitudes toward gendered divisions of work, masculinity/femininity constructs, and policy studies addressing role norms. Both German and international publications are relevant where they explicitly address gender roles. Exclude: studies focused solely on biological sex without addressing roles or norms.

pub_desc: Publications that address gender roles and the social expectations, behaviors and responsibilities associated with gender. Includes empirical articles, theoretical papers, books and reports on gender role attitudes, socialization, division of labor, family roles, workplace roles and intersections with health, education, and policy.
pub_narr: Include publications in German or other languages that explicitly study 'gender role' (singular) as a social construct: empirical studies measuring role endorsement, theoretical treatments of role concepts, historical or comparative analyses of gender role formation, and applied research linking gender role expectations to outcomes (health, employment, family life, identity). Include qualitative and quantitative work as well as policy reports. Exclude works that use the word 'role' in non-gender contexts (e.g. job role descriptions without reference to gender), purely biological sex-differences research that does not address social roles, and materials where 'role' appears only tangentially.

pub_desc: Publications on gender roles (plural), including research on stereotypes, normative expectations, role changes over time, cross-cultural comparisons, and the effects of gender roles on social outcomes.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, comparative and historical analyses, policy papers and qualitative research that explicitly investigate 'gender roles' as social norms, stereotypes, or patterns of behavior across contexts (family, work, education). Include cross-national comparisons and trend analyses of changing gender roles. Exclude publications that use the term in passing without substantive analysis, studies focused solely on biological sex differences without social role discussion, and irrelevant disciplinary uses of 'roles' (e.g. system roles in IT).

pub_desc: Publications covering health in broad sense: public health, epidemiology, health services, clinical studies, health policy, health behavior, and population health analyses.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, clinical reports, health policy analyses and books that focus on physical or population health, disease burden, prevention, health promotion, health care delivery and determinants of health. Include studies at individual and population levels, in German and other languages. Exclude non-health uses of 'gesundheit' (colloquial exclamation) and publications in unrelated domains (e.g. veterinary health unless explicitly about human health when relevant).

pub_desc: Publications on mental health and psychological wellbeing, including epidemiology of mental disorders, clinical psychiatry, psychotherapy research, public mental health, and studies of stress, wellbeing and mental health services.
pub_narr: Include empirical and review articles, clinical reports, policy analyses and books that address mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, stress, well-being), mental health services, determinants and interventions, and population-level mental health trends. Include both clinical and community-focused research. Exclude publications that deal solely with neurological disorders without psychiatric/psychological relevance or that mention 'psychisch' only peripherally.

pub_desc: Publications focusing on patient health, patient populations, patient experiences, clinical outcomes, patient safety, and health care delivery for patients.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, clinical reports, qualitative research and reviews that explicitly study patients: disease-specific patient cohorts, patient-reported outcomes, studies of patient pathways, care quality, satisfaction, adherence, and health outcomes in clinical populations. Exclude publications about general population health without a focus on patients or those that use 'patient' metaphorically.

pub_desc: Publications on workplace-based health, occupational health management, and company-level health promotion and prevention measures.
pub_narr: Relevant publications address health promotion, occupational safety and health (OSH) programs, workplace health policies, company-level interventions, organizational determinants of employee health, return-to-work programs, occupational health services, and evaluations of health promotion at the enterprise level. Include empirical studies, reviews, program descriptions, policy analyses, and economic evaluations focused on businesses, firms, factories, schools or other workplaces. Exclude publications limited to individual clinical care outside the workplace, general population health without connection to workplaces, purely clinical disease biology unrelated to occupational context, or publications solely about health care institutions unless framed as workplace health for staff.

pub_desc: Literature on health within the workplace: employee health status, working conditions, and in-company health interventions.
pub_narr: Include research on how work environment, organizational practices, and occupational exposures affect health of employees; studies evaluating workplace interventions (ergonomics, mental health programs, workplace wellness); surveillance reports of work-related illnesses and injuries; and qualitative work on employee perceptions of health at work. Exclude literature that discusses health in non-workplace contexts only, primary clinical research without workplace linkage, or studies of health systems not addressing workplace staff or conditions.

pub_desc: Studies and reports on the health of employees and other employed persons across occupations and sectors.
pub_narr: Include empirical research, reviews, surveillance reports, and policy analyses that focus on the physical, mental, and social health of workers. Topics include prevalence and determinants of work-related diseases, mental health among employees, absenteeism and presenteeism, occupational morbidity and mortality, and subgroup analyses by occupation, industry, gender, age. Exclude research on non-employed populations, clinical studies not addressing employment-related factors, or studies about employers' finances without health focus.

pub_desc: Publications on health complaints and symptom reports, including somatic and psychosomatic symptoms in working populations.
pub_narr: Include studies documenting prevalence, determinants, and consequences of self-reported health complaints (e.g., pain, fatigue, headaches, gastrointestinal symptoms, sleep problems), work-related symptom clusters, and clinical or survey-based assessments of symptom burden. Include research on reporting patterns, occupational antecedents of complaints, and intervention studies reducing symptom prevalence. Exclude purely diagnostic clinical case reports without relevance to population-level complaints, studies of laboratory biomarkers without symptom correlation, or publications focused only on major disease diagnoses unless symptoms are central.

pub_desc: Publications on violence in its various forms: interpersonal, domestic, workplace, sexual, political, and community violence.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, policy analyses, and program evaluations addressing causes, prevalence, risk factors, consequences, prevention, and intervention related to physical, sexual, psychological, and structural violence. Cover settings such as homes, schools, workplaces, public spaces, conflict zones, and institutions. Include studies on self-reported victimization, perpetration, bystander behavior, and service responses. Exclude literature solely on criminal procedure without health/social outcomes, animal violence not framed in human social research, or purely theoretical treatments with no empirical or applied focus unless they inform measurement or intervention.

pub_desc: Publications addressing violence involving children and adolescents (victimization, perpetration, exposure) across contexts such as family, school, peers, community, and online.
pub_narr: Include empirical articles, reviews, policy reports and book chapters that focus on physical, sexual, psychological, or relational violence where at least one party is a child or adolescent (typically ages ~0–19). Relevant topics: youth perpetration, youth victimization, exposure to domestic or community violence, bullying/cyberbullying, dating violence among adolescents, and prevention/intervention programs targeted at young people. Include studies from criminology, psychology, public health, education and social work. Exclude works that primarily address adult-only samples, large-scale armed conflict or terrorism when youth are not the primary focus, non-violent delinquency without a violence component, and purely theoretical pieces with no empirical or applied focus on youth.

pub_desc: Publications examining cross-national or global measures and comparisons of life satisfaction and subjective well‑being across populations and countries.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, comparative analyses, methodological papers, and reports that use or critique global measures of life satisfaction (e.g., Cantril ladder, single-item life satisfaction questions, SWLS) to compare countries, regions or population subgroups. Relevant topics: trends over time, determinants of national life satisfaction, happiness economics, cross-cultural measurement invariance, and policy implications. Exclude studies only focused on narrow clinical populations without broader subjective well‑being context, or purely theoretical discussions that do not engage with cross-national measurement or data.

pub_desc: Publications on health from a social-science and public-health perspective, including physical and mental health, health behaviors, healthcare access, and health determinants and outcomes.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, policy analyses, and public health reports addressing population health, disease burden, health inequalities, health behaviors (smoking, diet, exercise), mental health, healthcare utilization and access, health policy, and social determinants of health. Studies may be cross-sectional, longitudinal or intervention evaluations. Exclude purely molecular, cellular or bench-lab biomedical research that does not engage with population- or social-level health questions, veterinary health, or highly specialized clinical case reports lacking broader public-health relevance.

pub_desc: Publications on working from home / telework / remote work, focusing on effects for employees, organizations, work–life balance, productivity, ergonomics, and policy.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, literature reviews, case studies and policy analyses that examine home-based work arrangements (telework, remote work, work-from-home), their prevalence, determinants, effects on job performance, well-being, work–family conflict, organizational practices, digitalization, and occupational health/ergonomics. Include research on telework during COVID-19 and comparative analyses across sectors. Exclude publications solely about setting up home office furniture sales/retail, purely technical IT infrastructure guides without social or organizational analysis, or non-work-related home-office aesthetics.

pub_desc: Publications on immigration and migrants, covering migration flows, integration, policy, socioeconomic outcomes, health, and legal status.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews, policy analyses and theoretical works that address international migration, immigrant integration and assimilation, labor market outcomes of immigrants, refugee/asylum issues, migration policy and laws, remittances, transnationalism, and migrant health and education. Relevant disciplines: sociology, demography, economics, political science, public health and law. Exclude studies exclusively about internal migration (unless relevant), tourism travel statistics not related to migration, and purely historical migration narratives with no contemporary analytical relevance unless explicitly comparative.

pub_desc: Publications addressing social, economic, health, educational, gender, racial, and spatial inequalities, including theoretical analyses, empirical studies, reviews, and policy discussions.
pub_narr: Relevant publications examine inequality as a primary topic or present substantial empirical or theoretical treatment of disparities (income, wealth, poverty, labor market, health, education, gender, race/ethnicity, regional/urban-rural). Include comparative, cross-national, longitudinal, and case studies, and works that discuss causes, consequences, measurement, and policy responses. Exclude works where 'inequality' is only mentioned tangentially or used metaphorically without substantive analysis (e.g., brief mentions in unrelated topics), and exclude purely methodological papers with no application to social/economic disparities unless they introduce widely used measures of inequality (e.g., Gini) and discuss interpretation.

pub_desc: Scholarly works on trust in information, credibility of sources, information-seeking behavior, misinformation and disinformation, and the role of institutions and media in shaping public trust.
pub_narr: Include publications that investigate trust in information sources (news media, social media, governmental communications, experts), factors influencing perceived credibility, trust dynamics in digital environments, effects of misinformation, and interventions to build or measure trust in information. Empirical, theoretical, and review articles are relevant. Exclude papers where 'trust' refers to interpersonal trust unrelated to information exchange, or where information trust is only a passing phrase without substantive engagement.

pub_desc: Publications on information policy and information politics: regulation, governance, political use of information, transparency, information control, and the political implications of information flows and technologies.
pub_narr: Include works that address policies governing information (data protection, freedom of information, media regulation), the political uses of information and communication (propaganda, public diplomacy, surveillance, open government), and scholarly analyses of how information shapes political processes. Include normative, empirical, and legal studies focused on the politics of information. Exclude publications that only mention 'information' in technical contexts without linking to policy or political effects.

pub_desc: Publications on information and communication technologies (ICT): adoption, diffusion, digital skills, digital divide, ICT impacts on society, employment, education, and public services.
pub_narr: Include empirical and theoretical studies of ICT use, access, outcomes of digital technologies (internet, mobile, broadband, e‑government, ICT in education/workplaces), digital inequalities, policy evaluations of ICT programs, and societal implications of ICT proliferation. Exclude highly technical engineering papers focused on hardware design or low-level protocols when they lack social-science relevance to use, access, or impact.

pub_desc: Publications on political interest (interest in politics): its measurement, determinants, consequences for participation, civic engagement, political knowledge, and attitudes.
pub_narr: Include studies that focus on individual-level political interest or political attentiveness, its relationship with voting and other forms of participation, media consumption patterns, socialization, demographic correlates, and cross-national comparisons. Also include methodological work on measuring political interest. Exclude works where 'interest' refers to policy interest groups or institutional interests rather than individual political interest.

pub_desc: Publications that study individuals' interest or aspiration to assume leadership or supervisory roles. Includes empirical articles, reviews, theoretical papers and reports on leadership interest, leadership aspiration, desire for promotion, or intent to lead in organizational, educational or political settings.
pub_narr: Relevant publications explicitly address personal interest in leadership (e.g., leadership aspiration, willingness to lead, desire for managerial positions). Include cross-sectional and longitudinal empirical studies, theoretical treatments, and applied reports in German or English. Exclude works that only discuss leadership styles, team leadership effectiveness, organizational leadership structure, or leader traits without linking them to individuals' interest/aspiration to occupy leadership roles. Exclude studies focused solely on leadership training outcomes unless they measure pre-existing or changed interest in leadership.

pub_desc: Publications on work motivation: research about intrinsic and extrinsic motivation at work, employee engagement, motivational antecedents and outcomes, job design effects on motivation, and interventions to enhance workplace motivation.
pub_narr: Relevant publications explicitly address motivation in occupational contexts (paid work, volunteer work, internships). Include empirical studies, meta-analyses, theoretical frameworks (self-determination theory, expectancy theory), and applied evaluations of motivational interventions. Exclude studies of academic or school motivation unless directly tied to work contexts (e.g., vocational training). Exclude literature solely on job satisfaction unless motivation is a primary focus.

pub_desc: Publications investigating job satisfaction: conceptualizations, determinants (job characteristics, leadership, pay), consequences (performance, turnover, health), measurement issues, cross-cultural comparisons, and interventions to improve satisfaction.
pub_narr: Include empirical studies, reviews and theoretical works where job satisfaction is a primary variable or outcome. Accept workplace-focused research across sectors and populations (employees, volunteers). Include studies on overall and facet-specific job satisfaction. Exclude articles that mention satisfaction only peripherally or focus solely on unrelated outcomes without assessing job satisfaction.

pub_desc: Publications about adolescents (youth roughly aged 10–19): health, education, mental health, social behavior, risk behavior, development, and transition to adulthood. Includes empirical studies, reviews and policy reports focused on adolescent populations.
pub_narr: Relevant work centers on persons in adolescence (approximately ages 10–19, flexible to include lower/upper bounds in studies). Include research on physical and mental health, schooling, labor market entry, identity, family and peer influences, and youth policy. Exclude studies focusing solely on children under 10 or adults beyond adolescence unless data are disaggregated for adolescent subsamples.

pub_desc: Publications concerning children and adolescents (birth through late adolescence): research on development, health, education, family, mental health, socialization, and policy issues affecting minors.
pub_narr: Relevant publications explicitly target children (infancy, childhood) and/or adolescents (up to ~18–19 years). Include empirical studies, longitudinal cohorts, reviews, clinical and educational research, and policy analyses addressing developmental, health, psychosocial, and educational outcomes. Exclude studies exclusively on adult populations or animal studies. Where age ranges are broad, include only if results for children/young people are separately reported.

pub_desc: Publications addressing 'klima' (climate) in broad senses: atmospheric/climatic systems, climate change impacts, climate policy, climate science, climate perception and discourse. Includes empirical studies, reviews, theoretical work, and policy analyses in social and natural sciences.
pub_narr: Relevant publications are those whose primary topic is climate or climatic phenomena (e.g., temperature trends, precipitation patterns, climate modelling, climate policy, public perceptions of climate). Include interdisciplinary works linking climate to health, economics, agriculture, urban planning, and social responses. Exclude items where 'klima' appears only metaphorically or as a minor mention (e.g., office climate used solely as workplace atmosphere) unless the work explicitly treats atmospheric or socio-environmental climate. Include publications in German or English and both empirical and conceptual studies.

pub_desc: Publications specifically on 'klimawandel' (climate change): causes (anthropogenic and natural), impacts, mitigation, adaptation, vulnerability, policy responses, public perceptions, and communication of climate change.
pub_narr: Relevant works explicitly address climate change dynamics, evidence of warming, attribution studies, mitigation strategies (emission reduction, renewable energy), adaptation planning, socio-economic impacts, and public attitudes to climate change.
